item.title: Who Has Access to Claude? Bring AI Identity and Access Context Into Surface Command
item.description: Approving an AI service is only the starting point. As employees adopt Claude and their responsibilities change, security teams need to know who has access, which users hold administrative privileges, and whether those roles and group memberships still reflect the work they do. IBM’s 2025 Cost of a Data Breach Report found that, among studied organizations reporting an AI-related breach, 97% lacked proper AI access controls. item.title: シニアに向けた大情報時代におけるパソコン、スマホに対する心構えと実際にあった危ないと思った話

item.title: Suspected ransomware affiliate extradited to US over $500 million in extortion demands
item.description: A 43-year-old Kazakh national accused of helping a ransomware crew steal data from US hospitals and schools, then threatening to publish patients’ medical information, has been extradited from Italy, the US Department of Justice announced. Prosecutors believe Roman Khlynovskiy was a member of the “8-Digits Team,” a group affiliated with the INC and Lynx ransomware operations. item.title: Detectify launches Agentic Tooling to verify vulnerabilities in live applications
item.description: Detectify has launched Agentic Tooling. It lets organizations’ own AI agents, running in their own environments, proactively investigate suspected vulnerabilities and test whether they can be exploited in running applications. A new Security Ledger lets security teams verify agents’ findings against objective evidence, ensuring informed decisions rather than relying solely on probabilistic conclusions.
